name: RingCentral
description: RingCentral is a cloud communications platform for business calling, messaging, video collaboration, contact-center workflows, and communications administration. Organizations use it to connect employees and customers, operate phone systems, manage conversations, and review communications activity.
agentUseSummary: Connect one RingCentral extension with Relay-owned S256 PKCE OAuth, then let agents verify that exact extension, list at most ten first-page Simple call records, and inspect one record already present in that bounded set without exposing provider identities, names, raw phone numbers, detailed legs, recordings, communications actions, administration, other products, later pages, or raw APIs.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: The same three reads run without Relay per-action approval; exact extension binding, app permissions, fixed routes, bounds, audits, and secret isolation still apply.

providerSetup.nextAction: After batch integration, create or review the exact-permission RingCentral app, register the exact Railway callback, store credentials in staging, and validate state, omitted scope, S256 PKCE, returned permissions, single-use refresh replacement, exact extension binding, first-ten Simple call-log bounds, sensitive-field exclusion, response limits, rate-limit handling, session revocation, local deletion, and post-disconnect denial.

evidence.supports: RingCentral presents a cloud business-communications platform spanning calling, messaging, video collaboration, contact-center products, and communications administration.
RingCentral documents authorization-code OAuth with S256 PKCE, an ignored scope request parameter, access and single-use refresh tokens, and the current production authorization endpoint.
RingCentral documents app-configured permissions, including read-only ReadAccounts and ReadCallLog and the distinct ReadCallRecording permission that Relay excludes.
RingCentral documents Bearer token use, token invalidation, and session-wide revocation through the current revoke endpoint using confidential Basic client authentication.

RingCentral documents the self-extension call-log route, Simple versus Detailed views, provider identifiers, call metadata, parties, detailed legs, recordings, account-level access, and adjacent sensitive surfaces Relay excludes.
RingCentral documents per-app and per-user usage groups, customizable limits, HTTP 429 responses, Retry-After guidance, and the need to stop requests during a penalty interval.
RingCentral's API License Agreement governs API and SDK use, user data, distribution, marks, and related materials, so live release and official branding remain externally gated.
